preconditions.description: n is the number of workers (1 ≤ n ≤ 5000), and a, b are integers defining k = a/b (1 ≤ a ≤ b ≤ 10^5).

preconditions.expression: len(s) == n and all(c not in {'t', 'r', 'y', 'g', 'u', 'b'} for c in s)
preconditions.description: s is a string of length n with lowercase English letters excluding 't', 'r', 'y', 'g', 'u', 'b'.

postconditions.description: The output is a space-separated string where the first element is the count of obtainable job categories (c), followed by the sorted list of obtainable categories.

postconditions.expression: all(c in set(s) for c in obtainable_categories)
postconditions.description: All obtainable categories must exist in the original string s.

postconditions.expression: all(c in obtainable_categories for c in set(s) if is_obtainable(c, s, n, a, b))
postconditions.description: A category c is in obtainable_categories if and only if it is possible to make all workers have category c using the allowed operations.

postconditions.expression: is_obtainable(c, s, n, a, b) == (c == s[0] or can_unify_to(c, s, n, a, b))
postconditions.description: A category c is obtainable if either it is already the only category in s or it can be unified to by a sequence of valid operations.
